- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥0.8) and forecast is below recent low, adjust upward by 1–2% to avoid underestimating rebound.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤0.2) and forecast is above recent high, adjust downward by 1–2% to avoid overestimating recovery.
- If recent price has spiked (last 3–5 days > 10% above mean), reduce forecast peak by 5–10% to avoid overshoot.
- If sentiment is volatile (alternating ±0.4+), apply mean reversion bias: forecast = 0.8×last 7-day avg + 0.2×current forecast.
- For 30-day horizon, if true outcome deviates >5% from 14-day moving average, adjust forecast toward that average to reduce lag bias.
- If sentiment history shows consistent bullish momentum (e.g., 3+ consecutive +0.6+), reduce forecast slope to avoid over-optimism.
- If sentiment turns negative after a spike, apply “sudden drop” correction: subtract 3–5% from forecast 3–5 days after spike.
